title: Guided Star-Shaped Masked Diffusion
claim: Prior samplers make irreversible or undirected corrections; ours adds a learned error predictor so revisions target likely mistakes.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, same geometric trajectory with changing arrows per panel
description: Three side-by-side panels, labeled (a) MDLM, (b) Star, (c) G-Star, share the same background. It is a quarter-circle, fan-like set of shaded, curved bands in blue-grey, tan, pink and dark grey that stand for noise levels. A trajectory starts at x_T at the bottom left and passes through circular nodes x_{t+1}, x_t and x_0. In (a), dashed arrows go straight forward. They show an irreversible path. In (b), a solid arrow jumps to a dashed x_0 draft node. A wavy blue arrow labeled 'unguided remasking' returns to x_t, and a dashed arrow leads on to a new x_0. In (c), the layout is the same, but the wavy arrow is green and labeled 'guided remasking'. It lands in a different spot. The eye goes first to the colored wavy arrows, which mark where the panels differ.
caption: Pipeline comparison of MDLM, Star, and G-Star sampling. Each panel illustrates how a sampler moves from a noisy state xT toward a clean sample x0. (a) MDLM follows an irreversible trajectory: once a token is unmasked, it is copied forward and cannot be revised. (b) Star routes each transition through a fully denoised draft ˆx0 and then randomly remasks tokens, enabling revision but wasting refinement steps on already correct tokens. (c) G-Star uses the same star-shaped transition, but replaces random remasking with an error predictor gϕ that selectively remasks likely incorrect tokens. This targeted remasking focuses refinement on probable errors while preserving the stability of already plausible context.
abstract: The performance of pre-trained masked diffusion models is often constrained by their sampling procedure, which makes decisions irreversible and struggles in low-step generation regimes. We introduce a novel sampling algorithm that works with pre-trained models and, after a lightweight fine-tuning of a single layer, significantly improves sample quality and efficiency. Our method reformulates the generation process using a star-shaped paradigm, which inherently allows for error correction. To make this process effective, we augment it with a learnable re-masking scheduler that intelligently identifies and revises likely errors. This approach yields a substantial quality boost, particularly when using a small number of sampling steps. We extensively ablate key components of our approach and show its usability in different scenarios. In comprehensive experiments on text, and code generation, our sampling algorithm outperforms or matches existing methods.
